test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
This question is based on the five three-digit numbers given below.

573 136 357 442 814

(Example - 697 - First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

If 2 is added to the second digit of every

number, in how many numbers thus formed will the second digit be exactly divisible by the third digit?
solution:
Given: (left) 573 136 357 442 814 (right)

If 2 is added to the second digit of every number, the numbers become:

 
• 593 (573: 7+2 = 9)
 
• 156 (136: 3+2 = 5)
 
• 377 (357: 5+2 = 7)
 
• 462 (442: 4+2 = 6)
 
• 834 (814: 1+2 = 3)

Now, check which of these numbers have a second digit exactly divisible by the third digit:

 
• 593: 9 is not divisible by 3
 
• 156: 5 is not divisible by 6
 
• 377: 7 is divisible by 7
 
• 462: 6 is divisible by 2
 
• 834: 3 is divisible by 4

There are three such numbers (377, 462, and 834).

The correct answer is **"Option 4"**.
